FXUS62 KMFL 140750
AFDMFL

Area Forecast Discussion
National Weather Service Miami FL
350 AM EDT Wed Oct 14 2026

...New SHORT TERM, LONG TERM, MARINE...

.KEY MESSAGES...
Updated at 310 AM EDT Wed Oct 14 2026

 - Moisture gradually returns to the region today, with the 
   potential of a few showers south of Alligator Alley this 
   afternoon.

 - Afternoon apparent temperatures will increase from the upper
   90s today to 100-105F during the afternoon hours of Thursday
   and Friday.
 
 - The evolution of a frontal boundary will dictate our local
   weather this upcoming weekend. Confidence continues to increase
   for a forecast of windy and wet conditions for South Florida. 

&&

.SHORT TERM...
(Today through Thursday)
Issued at 310 AM EDT Wed Oct 14 2026

Another spectacular edition of fake fall is nearing a untimely 
conclusion across South Florida this morning as 07z mesoanalysis 
and GOES East water vapor imagery reveal that moisture is slowly
retrograding back into the region as deep-layer ridging remains
established to the north of our area. With an elongated mid-level
ridge draped across much of the southeastern United States, the
synoptic pattern across our region will remain rather benign. As
a surface ridge axis gradually slides eastward across the
southeastern United States and into the western Atlantic waters
today, surface wind flow will begin to veer to more of an easterly
direction as a frontolytic boundary over the Florida Keys and an
envelope of residual atmospheric moisture retrogrades back into
the region. Today still appears to be, very much so a transition 
day between the current dry airmass in place across South Florida 
this morning and more substantial moisture advection later in the
week. Breezy east-northeasterly flow and increasing moisture will
support the potential of afternoon shower activity south of
Alligator Alley today, where the best instability and moisture
will reside. Activity will remain vertically capped in nature as
moisture advection remains confined the the lowest level of the
boundary layer with a copious amount of dry air. The latest 
forecast continues to depict 20-40% rain chances across the 
southern half of the region this afternoon. Forecast high 
temperatures range from the upper 80s along the east coast to 
values in the low 90s across southwestern Florida.

Mid-level ridging briefly established across the southeastern 
United States is forecast to propagate eastward on Thursday as 
the next lobe of troughing slides eastward across the central 
United States. For now at least, our weather regime here in South
Florida will be primarily influenced by the surface ridge still
situated over the western Atlantic waters. Surface winds will 
gradually veer to an easterly direction by Thursday afternoon as 
the axis of surface ridging across the southeastern United States 
pivots further eastward and wanes in strength. Consequently, the 
established pressure gradient will begin to subside with surface 
winds remaining light out of an easterly direction. This will 
focus the best afternoon and evening rain chances across the 
western half of the peninsula on Thursday. Scattered showers and a
few thunderstorms remain possible, although weak lapse rates and
warm 500mb temperatures should keep the threat of strong
convection to a minimum. High temperatures on Thursday will 
remain similar to today (upper 80s to low 90s, peak values 
forecast, however the increase in moisture will result in a return
of apparent temperatures back into the 100-105F degree range 
during the late morning and early afternoon hours.

&&

.LONG TERM...
(Thursday night through Tuesday)
Issued at 310 AM EDT Wed Oct 14 2026


As the positively tilted trough amplifies and digs 
across the eastern half of the United States, a strengthening 
surface low will strengthen and push east-northeastward in 
tandem. A sprawling frontal boundary attached to the low is
forecast to push across the southeastern United States on Friday
before arriving across the region during the upcoming weekend. As
surface ridging slides further to the east, winds across South
Florida will begin to veer to a southeasterly component. This will
usher in even deeper atmospheric and continue the trend of 1)
higher rain chances and 2) higher apparent temperatures. Friday
could very well be the warmest day of the week with feels-like
temperatures once again reaching the 100-105F range across South
Florida. The breakdown of stronger background flow across the 
region will result in sea-breeze circulations being the driving 
mechanism of where afternoon convection focuses, which may reside
mainly across inland areas and Lake Okeechobee as both sea-breezes
converge inland. 

The placement of the aforementioned frontal boundary in relation to 
South Florida, surface high pressure axis to the north, and any 
mesoscale coastal convergence will have a direct influence on 
potential rainfall totals, wind gusts, and the severity of any 
marine/coastal impacts across the region during the upcoming weekend 
into next week. Forecasted precipitable water and low level RH 
values (via forecast soundings) during this time period appear to 
approach the daily max for this time of year, indicative of an 
airmass that is saturated in the low level boundary layer. 500mb 
temperatures are also forecast to be on the warmer side which may 
support an expansive warm cloud layer and heavy rainfall. The 
Weather Prediction Center has placed portions of the east coast of
South Florida in a Day 4 and Day 5 Marginal risk of excessive 
rainfall (Level 1 of 4). In this type of complex weather regime, 
it is far too early to discuss specific rainfall totals as
anchoring bias to specific values could hurt messaging more than
help it. The main takeaway is that forecast confidence is
increasing that heavy rainfall could occur across portions of
South Florida this weekend into early next week. Outside of any 
heavy rain threat, guidance has also been consistent in showing 
the enhancement of a pressure gradient across the western Atlantic
and South Florida. This would act to increase wind speeds across 
the area, resulting in gusty conditions and potential marine and 
coastal impacts. While forecast confidence has increased in a wet
and windy weekend, uncertainty as far as timing and impacts
remain. Stay tuned for forecast updates as we progress through the
remainder of the work week. An increase in wind and rain chances 
may keep ambient and apparent temperatures lower beginning during 
the upcoming weekend.

&&

.AVIATION...
(06Z TAFS)
Issued at 110 AM EDT Wed Oct 14 2026

Light and variable surface winds will prevail through daybreak
before breezy ENErly winds prevail across the region. Isolated
SHRA is possible in the vicinity of terminals south of Alligator
Alley today but confidence is too low to include VCSH in the TAFs
at this time. L/V winds forecast once again overnight with winds
quickly lessening in strength after sunset.

&&

.MARINE...
Issued at 310 AM EDT Wed Oct 14 2026

Breezy northeasterly winds will prevail across the local waters of 
South Florida through tonight. Small Craft Exercise Caution 
(SCEC) conditions could be realized at times across the Atlantic 
and Gulf waters as winds enhance and lessen with 
nocturnal/diurnal cycles. Waves will remain 2-3 feet across the 
region through early Thursday with the caveat that locally higher 
waves and winds are possible in and around any shower or 
thunderstorm activity, mainly across our southern waters. While 
uncertainty remains, forecast confidence continues to increase for
the potential of elevated seas and waves across the local waters 
of South Florida this weekend into early next week. 

&&
